title: Auto-responder residuals: TailLines not applied on the I1 resolution path, unattributed human-input sends, no plan-dialog drift alarm, and manifests false-matching their own patterns
summary: Four follow-ups from the plan-mode rule review, none blocking that landing. (1) TailLines is applied in decideAutoRespond but NOT in resolvePending/openPending, which match the pending pattern against the FULL pane — so for a tail-scoped rule a dialog that scrolled up still matches, prompt_cleared is under-reported, and sends land in no_effect/run_ended. Control-flow safe, but those outcomes are the evidence the measured auto-enforce sweep reads, so tail-scoped rules carry systematically skewed promotion evidence. openPending already resolves the rule by name, so threading the int through is a few lines. (2) human_input.go still logs 'sent keys' with no rule name, so under --human-input the new attribution is absent on exactly the path an operator watches. (3) No drift alarm for the plan rules: when the vendor reworks the dialog wording the rule goes inert and the symptom is the pre-fix hang. Non-urgent because it fails OPEN and self-limits to one lane (unlike the exhaustion case, which cost eight cycles of misattributed exit-81) — but its natural home is the teardown path beside warnExhaustionRegexDrift, so an exit-81 pane that looks plan-dialog-shaped names the drifted rule instead of dying generic. (4) PRE-EXISTING: feeding manifests/claude-tmux.json through the responder as if an agent rendered it fires cli_feedback_rating (send:0,Enter) and escalate:auth_recheck, because the manifest carries those patterns as DATA. The plan rules are immune (tail-windowed); the older rules are not. Also file: harvest the plan-file path disclosed in claude's dialog footer into the run dir so an auto-approved plan becomes gradeable evidence rather than discarded scrollback.
